items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: we got interested in Bing Crosby’s singing because he had a very nice voice... we enjoyed Bing’s style of jazz... It’s kind of like a tribute to him.

ctx.x: Wouldn’t do too much of that. Tell me about what inspired you to do an album about the music of Bing Crosby?

Well when I lived in Chicago we used to have a little record club, fellows that I knew, and we’d get together at this guy’s house. And we’d listen to the old Louis Armstrong records, the “Hot Five”s and the “Hot Seven”s and all of the things he made with Luis Russell. But also we got interested in Bing Crosby’s singing because he had a very nice voice. And we used to like to listen to him in the early days, when he was with John Scott Trotter’s orchestra, making recordings for Decca and before that, the other…
Great. You’ve mentioned the “Hot Five” and “Hot Seven” a couple of times. What was it about those particular recordings that really were such milestones, in your eyes?
